title: The Precision Cost of Limiting Imbalanced Assignments on a Four-Site Lipschitz Grid
banked_reason: Sound accepted angle-2 finite-game and four-site separation result is incremental; the general reviewer caps paper_score_ceiling at 5 below the field threshold 7.4, and independent validity audit finds no bounded same-assumption field-tier repair.
gap_reasons: The specified-analysis matching result in [Kallus (2018), Theorem 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.0531) does not settle this reconstruction-unrestricted experiment, but distinguishing those contracts alone supplies no general optimal-design characterization. The all-grid contribution is the observation-compatible finite reduction and exhaustive certification algorithm; the contact criterion does not determine which larger grids incur a balance cost. The substantive design separation is confined to four sites, with certificate bounds rather than evaluated sharp saddles or an explicitly characterized minimax procedure. The imbalance-budget theorem follows by conditioning on balanced assignments and supplies neither a matching achievable tradeoff nor the exact minimum imbalance needed for optimal precision. The current framing identifies these limitations and contains no stale assertion that the interior curve or larger-grid frontier is solved. The projected score is constrained by the single-grid substantive conclusion, unevaluated optimal tradeoff, and limited experimental guidance from an exhaustive algorithm on an idealized noiseless class. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

Replace the conditioning lower bound with a piecewise algebraic characterization of V_4(eta) on [0,1], supported by matching primal–dual certificates and explicit marginally fair designs and lifted reconstructions. Identify the exact budget at which unrestricted minimax precision becomes attainable.
proof_attempt_summary: The original exact four-site saddle and subsequent larger-grid paired-design and affine-estimator extensions did not produce a field-tier theorem. The accepted angle-2 contract delivered all-even observation-compatible finite-game equality and rational certification, a four-site exact-count-balance gap greater than 1/2500, necessary nonbalanced mass greater than 9/500, and an imbalance-budget lower frontier. Exact endpoint saddles, a matching interior tradeoff and the larger-grid frontier remain open; math review passed but independent validity audit confirmed incremental tier and no bounded field-tier repair.
tldr: At four sites, limiting the probability of a nonbalanced assignment below the certified threshold \(1-U_4/L_4>9/500\) has a strictly positive minimax precision cost for the causal mean contrast, even after optimizing every assignment law and every total Borel reconstruction. Specifically, \(V_4(\eta)-R(4)\ge(1-\eta)L_4-U_4\). This continuum tradeoff survives treatment marginal \(1/2\) at every site. Observation-compatible rounding proves an exact finite-path game and a terminating rational certificate algorithm for every even grid size. The structural balance frontier beyond four sites remains open.
gap: Bai (2022) and Kallus (2021) evaluate designs under specified analyses; Sudijono, Dobriban and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) optimize arbitrary reconstructions on outcome cubes. These results do not decide whether exact counts cost precision on a labeled Lipschitz grid.
fill: A rational four-site separation and a necessary nonbalanced-mass bound establish a concrete boundary. The open structural frontier asks when balanced designs can support a full-game saddle.
